spec: Write a function that returns the indices of all local minima in a list: positions (excluding the very first and last index) whose value is strictly less than both immediate neighbors. If the list has fewer than 3 elements, return an empty list.

Write a function that takes a sorted list of distinct integers and compresses it into a list of [start, end] pairs, one for each maximal run of consecutive integers (a single isolated value produces a pair where start equals end). An empty input returns an empty output.

Write a function that takes a list of lists, flattens it by exactly one level, and then removes duplicate values while preserving the order of first appearance. Any of the sublists, or the outer list, may be empty.

Write a function that splits a list into sublists wherever a given sentinel value occurs, similar to how a string split works, discarding the sentinel itself and keeping empty sublists that result from consecutive sentinels or sentinels at the ends. An empty input list returns a list containing one empty sublist.

Write a function that inserts a given separator value between every pair of consecutive elements of a list, leaving the list unchanged if it has 0 or 1 elements. The separator itself may equal an element already in the list.

Write a function that removes every falsy value (0, 0.0, empty string, empty list, None, and False) from a list, preserving the order of the remaining truthy elements. The input list may be empty or contain a mix of types.
Write a function that rotates a square matrix, given as a list of equal-length row lists, 90 degrees clockwise, returning a new matrix of the same dimensions. An empty matrix returns an empty matrix.

Write a function that finds all pairs of indices (i, j) with i less than j such that the elements at those indices in a list of integers add up to a given target sum, and returns the list of [i, j] pairs sorted by i then j. The input list may be empty or contain duplicate values.
Write a function that returns the number of distinct values present in a list. An empty list has 0 distinct values.

Write a function that groups the elements of a list of integers into a dictionary keyed by their remainder modulo a given positive integer n, where each key maps to the list of elements with that remainder in their original relative order, and keys with no matching elements are omitted. The input list may be empty.

Write a function that returns the average of each contiguous window of length k from a list of numbers, in order, rounded to 4 decimal places, as a list. If k is not a positive integer at most the length of the list, return an empty list.
Write a function that returns the index of the first occurrence of the maximum value in a non-empty list of numbers.
Write a function that returns the index of the first occurrence of the minimum value in a non-empty list of numbers.

Write a function that takes a list of numbers and returns a new list of the same values but with alternating signs applied: the element at even index (0, 2, 4, ...) is made positive (its absolute value) and the element at odd index (1, 3, 5, ...) is made negative (the negative of its absolute value). The input list may be empty.

Write a function that returns the length of the longest common prefix shared by two lists, i.e. the number of leading positions at which the two lists have equal elements before the first mismatch (or before either list ends). Either list may be empty, giving a result of 0.

Write a function that returns the length of the longest common suffix shared by two lists, i.e. the number of trailing positions at which the two lists have equal elements before the first mismatch (scanning from the end), or before either list is exhausted. Either list may be empty, giving a result of 0.

Write a function that splits a list of non-negative numbers into consecutive chunks such that the sum of each chunk does not exceed a given limit, adding elements to the current chunk greedily and starting a new chunk when adding the next element would exceed the limit. Assume every individual element is less than or equal to the limit; the input list may be empty.

Write a function that takes a list of lists and interleaves them round-robin: it takes the first element of each sublist in order, then the second element of each, and so on, skipping any sublist once it is exhausted. The outer list or any sublist may be empty.

Write a function that returns the elements of the first list that remain after removing one matching occurrence for each occurrence of that value found in the second list (a multiset difference), preserving the relative order of the surviving elements from the first list. Either input list may be empty.

Write a function that splits a list into consecutive chunks of a given size k (the last chunk may be smaller), then reverses the order of the chunks themselves (not the elements within each chunk), and concatenates them back into a flat list. Assume k is a positive integer; the input list may be empty.

Write a function that pads a list on the right with a given fill value until it reaches a target length n, or truncates it down to the first n elements if it is already longer than n. If the list is already exactly length n, it is returned unchanged.

Write a function that pads a list on the left with a given fill value until it reaches a target length n. If the list is already longer than n, it is truncated by removing elements from the left, keeping the last n elements. If already exactly length n, it is returned unchanged.
Write a function that counts how many times each distinct value appears in a list and returns the counts as a dictionary mapping value to count. An empty list returns an empty dictionary.

Write a function that returns a list of [value, count] pairs describing each distinct value in a list and how many times it occurs, sorted by count in descending order, breaking ties by the value in ascending order. An empty list returns an empty output.

Write a function that returns the maximum possible sum of any contiguous window of exactly k elements in a list of numbers. Assume k is a positive integer no greater than the length of the (non-empty) list.

Write a function that returns the minimum possible sum of any contiguous window of exactly k elements in a list of numbers. Assume k is a positive integer no greater than the length of the (non-empty) list.
Write a function that returns the first element in a list that occurs exactly once anywhere in the list, scanning from the start. If every element repeats, return None. The input list may be empty.
Write a function that returns the last element in a list (scanning from the end) that occurs exactly once anywhere in the list. If every element repeats, return None. The input list may be empty.
Write a function that removes the elements of a list between two given indices, start (inclusive) and end (exclusive), and returns the resulting list. Assume 0 <= start <= end <= length of the list.

Write a function that inserts a given value into a list at a specified index, shifting subsequent elements to the right, and returns the resulting list. Assume 0 <= index <= length of the list (index equal to the length appends at the end).

Write a function that interleaves two lists, alternately taking an element from the first list in its original order and an element from the second list in reversed order, starting with the first list; once one side runs out, the remaining elements from the other side (still following its own order) are appended. Either list may be empty.
Write a function that counts how many elements at the start of a list are equal to the first element, stopping at the first element that differs. An empty list returns 0.
Write a function that counts how many elements at the end of a list are equal to the last element, stopping at the first element (scanning backward) that differs. An empty list returns 0.

Write a function that repeatedly removes adjacent pairs of equal elements from a list (like collapsing a stack: pushing each element, but popping the previous one instead if it equals the current element) until no more adjacent pairs are equal, and returns the remaining elements in order. An empty list returns an empty list.

Write a function that, given a list of integers and an inclusive range [lo, hi], returns a sorted list of every integer in that range that does not appear in the list. Values in the list outside the range are ignored, and the list may be empty or contain duplicates.
Write a function that computes the alternating sum of a list of numbers: the first element added, the second subtracted, the third added, and so on. An empty list has an alternating sum of 0.

Write a function that splits a list of integers into consecutive groups such that all elements in a group share the same even/odd parity, starting a new group whenever the parity changes, and returns the list of groups. An empty input returns an empty list of groups.

Write a function that shifts a list to the right by k positions, dropping the last k elements and filling the first k positions with a given fill value, returning a new list of the same length. Assume k is non-negative; if k is greater than or equal to the list length, the result is entirely filled with the fill value.

Write a function that pairs up the elements of two lists positionally into a list of [x, y] pairs, stopping as soon as the shorter list is exhausted (like the built-in zip function). Either list may be empty, giving an empty result.

Write a function that interleaves two lists in alternating chunks of size k: it takes the next k elements from the first list, then the next k from the second, and so on, continuing to pull chunks from whichever list still has elements once the other is exhausted. Assume k is a positive integer; either list may be empty.
